name: Perceived width from narrow↔wide juxtaposition, real double-tracked (not cloned) hard pans, and a mono-safe stereo bed: mid-side EQ that nearly kills the mids on a send, plus reverb that decorrelates only the sides while the dry center stays untouched
goal: Make a mix feel dramatically wide without master-bus wideners or phase-wrecked lows: write and arrange moments that open from narrower sections (juxtaposition), pan two real performances of the same part L/R (not a flipped copy), and for bass/beds use mid-side processing so the center stays dry and mono while only the sides get EQ lift and reverb. Delta vs stereo-width cluster: treats width as an arrangement/timing contrast first, insists on true double-tracks for L/R pan width, and the concrete M/S recipe of ~−30 dB mid cut on a parallel path plus dry-center / wet-sides reverb for mono-compatible stereo bass.

source.title: Get A Wide Mix Without Any Issues!

prerequisites: DAW with mid-side EQ (or mid-side encode/decode), panning, a reverb return, and sidechain/ducking optional
Two real takes or differently processed layers of the same part (not identical clones)

inputs.name: mix
inputs.description: Multitrack mix with at least one part that can open wide

outputs.name: wide_mix
outputs.description: Mix that feels wider in sections while mono fold-down stays solid

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Do not put a stereo widener on the master bus as the main width strategy.
Never pan a bit-identical clone hard L/R and expect width — it collapses to mono.
Keep true mono energy (kick, sub, lead vocal) centered.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.
Steady pitch: leave out intentional pitch-drift LFOs unless the brief asks for tape wobble (Matt prefers steady pitch).

steps.action: Audit the arrangement: if everything is always wide, listeners adapt and nothing feels immersive. Plan narrower (near-mono) sections that precede the wide moments so the spread reads as a change.

For L/R width on a featured layer (e.g. vocals, guitars): use two real performances or differently processed takes of the same line and pan them apart (source example ~30 either way). A/B against a hard-panned clone of one take — the clone will not create the same image.
steps.expect: True stereo image from decorrelated takes

steps.action: Build a mono-safe stereo bed for bass or a dense layer: send or parallel-process through a mid-side EQ and cut the mid channel hard (source: about −30 dB) so almost only sides remain on that path; optionally lift selected side bands. The dry center path keeps the mono power.
steps.expect: Sides carry width; center stays solid

steps.action: Feed that sides-heavy path into a reverb so the sides gain space while the middle stays completely dry and raw — mono fold-down still has the dry center.
Optional: light sidechain from drums into competing wide layers so mono-focused hits still punch. Check the whole mix in mono.
steps.expect: Wide sections survive mono; kick/sub intact

verification: A narrow section followed by a wide section audibly expands.
Hard-panned real doubles stay wide; identical clones do not.
Mono fold-down keeps bass/center level; no hollow pumping.
